summary:
Astrion Multi-Epoch Sky Explorer is an interactive, browser-based astronomical exploration platform that transforms complex multi-epoch sky observations into an accessible visual experience. It enables users to search for celestial targets, explore observations across different times, compare astronomical images, and identify apparent changes in object positions.
By combining automated sky-field generation, multi-epoch visualization, and motion detection, Astrion provides an accessible way to explore how the sky changes over time.
details:
HOW IT WORKS:
·      Cosmic Welcome Interface: Provides an interactive welcome experience with user onboarding and role selection.

·      Target Search: Allows users to search for celestial objects using object names or Right Ascension (RA) and Declination (Dec) coordinates.

·      Automated Sky-Field Generation: Generates consistent astronomical sky fields and moving-target trajectories across multiple Modified Julian Date (MJD) epochs.

·      Multi-Epoch Exploration: Enables users to inspect individual observation views and examine celestial targets across different epochs.

·      Comparative Analysis: Provides side-by-side comparisons of observations, including Epoch 1 and Epoch 5.

·      Change Detection: Generates automated difference maps to highlight changes between observations and reveal apparent target movement.

KEY BENEFITS & IMPACT:

·      Makes complex astronomical observation concepts more accessible to non-specialists.

·      Empowers students, educators, and citizen scientists to explore astronomical phenomena.

·      Demonstrates automated visualization and tracking of moving celestial objects.

·      Encourages scientific curiosity through interactive astronomical exploration.

·      Introduces users to coordinate-based searching, observation timelines, and comparative sky analysis.

TOOLS & TECHNOLOGIES:

·      Python: Core programming language and backend application logic.

·      Streamlit: Interactive web dashboard and user-interface development.

·      Astropy: Astronomical image normalization using Asinh Stretch.

·      Matplotlib: High-resolution astronomical image rendering and visualization.

·      NumPy: Numerical calculations and data processing.

·      GitHub: Source code management and deployment workflow.

Streamlit Cloud: Application hosting and online accessibility.

CREATIVE ELEMENTS:

·      Combines astronomical visualization, target searching, and multi-epoch comparison within one interactive platform.

·      Generates consistent simulated sky fields to demonstrate changes in celestial observations over time.

·      Uses automated difference maps to make apparent object movement easier to identify.

·      Incorporates direct text labels to improve the interpretation of astronomical images.

·      Provides multiple exploration modes through individual views, comparisons, and change detection.

·      Uses a high-resolution visualization approach with 300 × 300 rendering, bicubic smoothing, and direct target labeling.

USE OF ARTIFICIAL/SUPER INTELLIGENCE (AI/SI)

AI tools assisted the development process through technical planning, architecture design, code optimization, and presentation preparation.

·      AI-Assisted Architecture: Supported the development of application structure and technical planning.

·      Code Optimization: Assisted with coding ideas, debugging, and improving development efficiency.

·      Project Structuring: Helped organize the technical workflow and presentation narrative.

Human Direction: The project's objectives, scientific direction, design decisions, and final implementation were guided and reviewed by the team.
